_: A vendor's REST API, read with a key (apireads.py): each row is the base (or the card's own address for a self-hosted one), how the key rides (bearer / header+format / query / basic, or google / graph: the app's own sign-ins), the cheap GET the card's Test makes, and the vendor's page it was read off (2026-11-08). The Connections page reads the same rows.

digitalocean.title: DigitalOcean
digitalocean.desc: Droplets, apps, databases, domains and billing as reports and an agent tool - GET /v2/droplets, /v2/apps, /v2/customers/my/balance.

terraform_cloud.title: Terraform Cloud
terraform_cloud.desc: Workspaces, runs and their state as reports and an agent tool - GET /organizations/<org>/workspaces, /workspaces/<id>/runs.

better_stack.title: Better Stack
better_stack.desc: Uptime monitors, incidents and on-call as reports and an agent tool - GET /monitors, /incidents.

circleci.title: CircleCI
circleci.key_page: app.circleci.com → User settings → Personal API Tokens
circleci.desc: Pipelines, workflows and failed jobs as reports and an agent tool - GET /project/<slug>/pipeline, /workflow/<id>/job.

buildkite.title: Buildkite
buildkite.key_page: buildkite.com → Personal settings → API access tokens
buildkite.desc: Builds, pipelines and agents as reports and an agent tool - GET /organizations/<org>/builds?state=failed.

coda.title: Coda
coda.key_page: coda.io → Account settings → API settings → Generate API token
coda.desc: Docs, tables and rows as reports and an agent tool - GET /docs, /docs/<id>/tables/<table>/rows.

intrinio.title: Intrinio
intrinio.desc: Company data, fundamentals and prices as reports and an agent tool - GET /companies/<ticker>, /securities/<ticker>/prices.

benzinga.title: Benzinga
benzinga.desc: Market news and calendars as reports and an agent tool - GET /news?tickers=AAPL, /calendar/earnings.

tradier.title: Tradier
tradier.desc: Quotes, option chains, balances and positions as reports and an agent tool - read only: no order is ever placed from this card.

diffbot.title: Diffbot
diffbot.desc: A web page read into clean article text and fields - GET /v3/article?url=<page>, /v3/analyze?url=<page>.

jenkins.title: Jenkins
jenkins.key_page: Jenkins → your name → Configure → API Token
jenkins.desc: Jobs, builds and their console as reports and an agent tool - GET /api/json, /job/<name>/lastBuild/api/json.

sonarqube.title: SonarQube
sonarqube.key_page: SonarQube → My Account → Security → Generate token
sonarqube.desc: Quality gates, issues and coverage as reports and an agent tool - GET /api/qualitygates/project_status?projectKey=<key>.

elastic.title: Elasticsearch
elastic.desc: Indices, cluster health and search results as reports and an agent tool - GET /_cat/indices?format=json, /<index>/_search?q=...

splunk.title: Splunk
splunk.desc: Saved searches, their results and server health as reports and an agent tool, over the management port (8089).

dynatrace.title: Dynatrace
dynatrace.key_page: Dynatrace → Access tokens → Generate new token
dynatrace.desc: Problems, entities and metrics as reports and an agent tool - GET /api/v2/problems, /api/v2/metrics/query?metricSelector=...

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
kubernetes.desc: Namespaces, pods, deployments and events as reports and an agent tool - GET /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods. Reads only.

google_drive.title: Google Drive
google_drive.desc: Find and list files in your Google Drive with the Google Sheets card's sign-in - GET /files?q=name contains 'budget'. Nothing to paste here.

onedrive.title: OneDrive
onedrive.desc: Find and list files in your OneDrive with the Outlook card's Microsoft sign-in - GET /me/drive/root/children, /me/drive/root/search(q='budget').

office365_files.title: Microsoft 365 files
office365_files.desc: Files shared with you across OneDrive and SharePoint, with the Outlook card's Microsoft sign-in - GET /me/drive/sharedWithMe, /sites?search=...

docker_hub.title: Docker Hub
docker_hub.key_page: Docker Hub, your account settings, Personal access tokens
docker_hub.desc: Repositories, tags and pull counts as reports and an agent tool - the token is swapped for a short-lived one, then GET /v2/namespaces/<you>/repositories.

uptimerobot.title: UptimeRobot
uptimerobot.desc: Monitors, their uptime and alert contacts as reports and an agent tool - UptimeRobot's reads are POSTs (getMonitors), and only those are sent.

heroku.title: Heroku
heroku.key: API key or an authorization token
heroku.key_page: Heroku, Account settings, API Key (or heroku authorizations:create)
heroku.desc: Apps, dynos, releases and add-ons as reports and an agent tool - GET /apps, /apps/<app>/dynos, /apps/<app>/releases.

gcp.title: Google Cloud
gcp.key_page: Google Cloud console, IAM, Service accounts, Keys, Add key (JSON) - give it the Viewer role
gcp.desc:
Projects, Cloud Run services, Cloud Functions and logs as reports and an agent tool - the path names the service: /run/v2/projects/

/locations/-/services, POST /logging/v2/entries:list.

browserbase.title: Browserbase
browserbase.desc: Cloud browsers for agents: list projects and sessions, and start a session (POST /sessions) whose connect URL an agent drives. Nothing else is sent.

oxylabs.title: Oxylabs
oxylabs.key_page: the Oxylabs dashboard, Web Scraper API, Users
oxylabs.desc: Web pages and search results fetched through Oxylabs' scraper - POST /v1/queries starts a fetch, GET /v1/queries/<id>/results reads it; /v2/stats is the usage.

brightdata.title: Bright Data
brightdata.key_page: the Bright Data control panel, Account settings, API keys
brightdata.desc: A page or a search result fetched through your Web Unlocker or SERP zone - POST /request with {zone, url, format}; GET /zone/get_active_zones lists the zones.

plaid.title: Plaid
plaid.desc: Balances, transactions, holdings and liabilities of an account already linked to your Plaid app - you paste the Item's access token; no Link screen here. Reads only.

ibkr.title: Interactive Brokers
ibkr.host_hint: https://localhost:5000/v1/api, the Client Portal gateway on this computer
ibkr.desc: Accounts, positions, balances and quotes through your own Client Portal gateway - GET /portfolio/accounts, /portfolio/<id>/positions/0. Reads only: no order is ever placed from this card.

schwab.title: Charles Schwab
schwab.key_page: your app at developer.schwab.com, after one sign-in to it
schwab.desc: Accounts, positions, orders placed elsewhere and quotes - GET /trader/v1/accounts?fields=positions, /marketdata/v1/quotes?symbols=AAPL. Reads only: no order is ever placed from this card.

bamboohr.title: BambooHR
bamboohr.key_page: BambooHR, your name, API Keys (an admin may need to allow it)
bamboohr.desc: The employee directory, time off and reports as reports and an agent tool - GET /employees/directory, /time_off/whos_out. Your BambooHR admin gives API access.

netsuite.title: NetSuite
netsuite.key_page: NetSuite: your admin makes an integration record (token-based auth) and an access token for a read-only role
netsuite.desc: Records and SuiteQL queries as reports and an agent tool - POST /services/rest/query/v1/suiteql {q: "SELECT ..."}, GET /services/rest/record/v1/vendor. Token-based auth from your NetSuite admin.

sap.title: SAP
sap.host_hint: https://my-s4.example.com (or the API host your BTP gives)
sap.key: password of the communication user, or the OAuth client secret
sap.key_page: your SAP admin: a communication arrangement for the APIs you read, with a read-only communication user
sap.desc: S/4HANA OData reads as reports and an agent tool - business partners, purchase orders, journal entries: GET /sap/opu/odata/sap/<service>/<entity>?$format=json. Your SAP admin gives the communication user.

dynamics365.title: Dynamics 365
dynamics365.key: client secret of your company's own app
dynamics365.key_page: your company's own app in Microsoft Entra, Certificates and secrets - added in Power Platform admin as an application user with a read-only role
dynamics365.desc: Dataverse tables - accounts, contacts, opportunities, cases - as reports and an agent tool: GET /api/data/v9.2/accounts?$top=10. Your own company app; Taskuary ships none.

workday.title: Workday
fields: integration system user (ISU@tenant), for basic sign-in
workday.key: the ISU's password, or the API client's refresh token
workday.key_page: your Workday admin: an integration system user with a read-only security group, or an API client with a refresh token
workday.desc: Workers, organizations and custom reports (RaaS) as reports and an agent tool - GET /ccx/api/v1/<tenant>/workers, /ccx/service/customreport2/<tenant>/<owner>/<report>?format=json.

adp.title: ADP
fields: TLS certificate file (.pem) on this computer
adp.key_page: ADP API Central (or your ADP partner app) - it also issues the TLS certificate the calls need
adp.desc: Workers, pay statements and time cards as reports and an agent tool - GET /hr/v2/workers. ADP needs its TLS client certificate on every call: your ADP admin gives the client id, secret and certificate.

epic.title: Epic (EMR)
epic.host_hint: the FHIR R4 base your Epic organization gives (https://.../api/FHIR/R4)
fields: key id (kid), if the org asks
epic.key: private key (PEM) whose public key the organization registered
epic.key_page: the Epic organization's admin: they register your backend app and its public key, and grant it the FHIR reads it may make
epic.desc: FHIR R4 reads - Patient, Encounter and what the organization grants - with SMART backend services: a JWT signed with your key, no sign-in screen. Reads only, scoped by the org.

cerner.title: Oracle Cerner (EMR)
fields: key id (kid), if the org asks
cerner.key: private key (PEM) whose public key the organization registered
cerner.key_page: the organization's Oracle Health admin: they register your system account and its public key, and grant it the FHIR reads it may make
cerner.desc: FHIR R4 reads - Patient, Encounter and what the organization grants - with SMART backend services: a JWT signed with your key, no sign-in screen. Reads only, scoped by the org.

pointclickcare.title: PointClickCare (EMR)
pointclickcare.key: refresh token the organization's sign-in gave your partner app
pointclickcare.key_page: PointClickCare's partner program: your app is approved, and the organization signs in to it once
pointclickcare.desc: Facilities, residents and their census as reports and an agent tool, through PointClickCare's partner API - your partner app, approved by PointClickCare and signed in to once by the organization. Reads only.

box.title: Box
box.desc: Your Box files for the agents and reports, read with your own sign-in - GET /search?query=budget, /folders/0/items, /files/<id>. Reads only.

oauth.console: the Box Developer Console (app.box.com/developers/console): Create Platform App, choose User Authentication (OAuth 2.0), and tick Read all files and folders

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.desc: Your Zoom meetings and cloud recordings for the agents and reports - GET /users/me/meetings, /users/me/recordings?from=2026-11-01. Reads only.

oauth.console: marketplace.zoom.us: Develop, then Build App - a General App, managed by the user - with the meeting and recording read scopes

zoom_chat.title: Zoom Team Chat
zoom_chat.desc: Zoom Team Chat direct messages, and channel messages that @mention you, land on your work rail through triage. People in your Zoom account are colleagues; an outside contact is a stranger.

oauth.console: marketplace.zoom.us: Develop, then Build App - a General App, managed by the user - with the team chat read scopes (sessions, messages, users)

webex.title: Webex
webex.desc: Webex direct messages, and space messages that @mention you, land on your work rail through triage. People in your Webex organization are colleagues; anyone else is a stranger.

oauth.console: developer.webex.com: My Webex Apps, then Create a New App - an Integration - with the people, rooms and messages read scopes

threads.title: Threads
threads.desc: Replies to your Threads posts and posts that mention you land on your work rail through triage - always as a stranger's words: Threads has no colleagues.

oauth.console: developers.facebook.com/apps: create an app with the Access the Threads API use case, and add the redirect address under its Threads settings

hubspot.title: HubSpot
hubspot.desc: HubSpot tickets and tasks assigned to you land on your work rail through triage, and agents read any CRM record - GET /crm/v3/objects/contacts, /crm/v3/objects/deals/<id>.

oauth.scopes: oauth tickets crm.objects.owners.read crm.objects.contacts.read crm.objects.companies.read crm.objects.deals.read
oauth.console: developers.hubspot.com: your developer account, then Apps, then Create app - its Auth tab holds the keys and the redirect URL

salesforce.title: Salesforce
salesforce.desc: Salesforce cases and tasks assigned to you land on your work rail through triage, and agents read any record - GET /services/data/v62.0/query?q=SELECT Id, Name FROM Account.

oauth.console: Salesforce Setup: App Manager, then New Connected App - enable OAuth with the api and refresh_token scopes

docusign.title: DocuSign
docusign.desc: DocuSign envelopes waiting on your signature land on your work rail through triage, and agents read an envelope's status - GET /envelopes/<id>, /envelopes/<id>/recipients.

oauth.console: DocuSign Admin: Apps and Keys, then Add App and Integration Key - add a secret key and the redirect URI

basecamp_todos.title: Basecamp to-dos
basecamp_todos.desc: Basecamp to-dos assigned to you, and Pings and @mentions in your Hey! menu, land on your work rail through triage. Your team is known; a client is a stranger.

mailgun.title: Mailgun
mailgun.host_hint: https://api.mailgun.net, or https://api.eu.mailgun.net for an EU account
fields: receiving domain - the one your route stores mail for
mailgun.key_page: app.mailgun.com, in the API Security page of your account menu
mailgun.desc: Mail your Mailgun route stores lands on your work rail through triage - Taskuary polls Mailgun's stored messages, so no public address is needed.

sendgrid.title: SendGrid Inbound Parse
fields: signature verification key (optional - from the Inbound Parse security policy)
sendgrid.key_page: app.sendgrid.com, in the API Keys page under Settings
sendgrid.desc: Mail SendGrid Inbound Parse receives lands on your work rail through triage. SendGrid pushes it, so it needs a public address that reaches this computer - your own tunnel.

line.title: LINE
fields: channel secret - the Basic settings tab
line.key_page: the LINE Developers Console, on your Messaging API channel's Messaging API tab
line.desc: Messages to your LINE Official Account land on your work rail through triage - as a stranger's words. LINE pushes them, so it needs a public address that reaches this computer - your own tunnel.

substack.title: Substack
substack.desc: Your publication's posts, read from its public feed, for the agents and reports. Substack has no API: replies and comments reach you as Substack's own emails, through your mail card.
